summary: A deadlock occurs when processes are blocked, each holding a resource and waiting for another. Four necessary Coffman conditions must hold simultaneously: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. Deadlocks can be analyzed using a Resource Allocation Graph (RAG). Operating systems handle deadlocks through prevention, avoidance (such as the Banker's algorithm), detection and recovery, or ignorance (the ostrich algorithm). A safe state allows resource allocation in a safe sequence to avoid deadlock, while an unsafe state may lead to one.

key_terms.definition: A situation where a set of processes are blocked because each holds a resource and waits for another.
Four necessary conditions that must hold at the same time for a deadlock to occur.
At least one resource is non-sharable, so only one process can use it at a time.
A process holds at least one resource while waiting to acquire additional resources held by other processes.
A resource can be released only voluntarily by the process holding it.
A set of processes waiting for resources in a circular chain.
A directed graph with process nodes and resource nodes used to represent resource requests and assignments.
An avoidance algorithm used by the OS to decide whether to grant a request.
A state in which the system can allocate resources to every process in some order and still avoid deadlock.
A state that does not always lead to deadlock, but may.
